children: InMed Pharmaceuticals Inc. reported a fiscal 2026 net loss, with revenue of $3.18M largely from discontinued BayMedica commercial operations and a net loss attributable to common shareholders of $13M; diluted loss per share was ($3.12) for the year — 10-K Summary.
Revenue was $3.18M for FY 2026, down from $4.94M in FY 2025; YoY change (35.7%).
Net income (loss) attributable to common shareholders was a loss of $13.0M for FY 2026, versus a loss of $8.16M in FY 2025; YoY change (59.1%).
Diluted earnings per share (basic & diluted) was a loss of $3.12 for FY 2026, compared with a loss of $8.36 in FY 2025.

Pipeline focus: The company is advancing three novel chemical entity programs — INM-901 (Alzheimer’s), INM-089 (dry AMD) and INM-755 (epidermolysis bullosa) — and has shifted strategic priorities toward preclinical R&D.
Commercial shift: Management completed a wind down of BayMedica commercial operations due to regulatory risk, leaving the company with preclinical-only activities and limited commercial revenue.
Operational milestone: Completed a Phase 2 trial for INM-755 that showed exploratory anti-itch signals; manufacturing capabilities include the IntegraSyn platform.
Corporate transaction: The company signed a merger agreement with Mentari to combine businesses, a deal expected to materially change ownership and strategic direction.
Liquidity risk: Cash runway was projected into Q3 2026 absent the merger; continued R&D and operations depend on securing additional financing or closing the transaction.
